It renders a <button> labelled `Count: N` (an unrelated counter that increments on click) and a <ul> with one <li> per item sorted ascending as numbers WITHOUT mutating the `items` prop. The sorting must run inside useMemo, keyed on `items`, and call onCompute() each time it actually runs — so clicking the counter must NOT call onCompute again, while passing a new items array must.

testCases.description: Renders the items sorted ascending without mutating the prop
Clicking the counter does not recompute the sorted list
testCases.expected: button 'Count: 2'; onCompute called 1 time in total

testCases.description: A new items array does recompute it

complexityExplanation: Sorting a copy of the items array costs O(n log n) time and O(n) extra space, and useMemo avoids recomputation on unrelated state changes.

title: Simple Data Table
promptSeed: Build SimpleTable({ columns, rows }) where columns is [{ key, label }] and rows is an array of objects. Render a <table> with a <thead> row of <th> cells showing each label, and a <tbody> with one <tr> per row and one <td> per column showing String(row[column.key]) (an empty string for a missing/undefined/null value). When rows is empty render a single <tr> with one <td colSpan={columns.length}> reading 'No rows'.

testCases.description: Renders one header cell per column label
Renders one row per item with cells in column order
Missing, undefined and null values render as empty cells
An empty table shows a single "No rows" cell spanning all columns

complexityExplanation: The table renders each column header once and each cell once, requiring R*C cell operations plus O(C) header work.

title: useHistory: Undo / Redo
promptSeed: Write useHistory(initial, limit = 100) returning { state, set, undo, redo, canUndo, canRedo }. set(valueOrUpdater) pushes a new present state (an updater function receives the current state); setting a value that is Object.is-equal to the current one does nothing. undo() moves to the previous state and redo() back; both do nothing at the ends. Calling set() after undo discards the redo branch. At most `limit` past states are kept (the oldest are dropped). set/undo/redo keep a stable identity.

testCases.description: Starts with the initial state and nothing to undo or redo
undo and redo do nothing at the ends
testCases.input: undo() then redo() on a fresh history

testCases.description: set pushes a new state and enables undo
undo and redo walk back and forth
testCases.input: useHistory(0): set(1), set(2), undo, undo, redo

testCases.description: set after undo discards the redo branch
set accepts an updater function and ignores an unchanged value
testCases.expected: state 5; canUndo false (the repeated 6 added nothing)

testCases.description: limit drops the oldest history entries
set, undo and redo keep a stable identity

complexityExplanation: All operations (set, undo, redo) manipulate only the ends of bounded past/future buffers, giving constant‑time work while storing at most limit states, i.e., linear space in the limit.

title: Virtualized (Windowed) List
promptSeed: Build VirtualList({ items, itemHeight, height, overscan = 3 }) for long lists of strings. Render <div role="list" style={{ height, overflowY: 'auto', position: 'relative' }} onScroll> containing ONE inner <div> whose style.height is items.length * itemHeight (the full scroll height, position: relative). Inside it render only the visible window: items from max(0, floor(scrollTop / itemHeight) - overscan) up to min(items.length, ceil((scrollTop + height) / itemHeight) + overscan), each as <div role="listitem"> with style position: absolute, top: index * itemHeight, height: itemHeight and the item text. Track scrollTop from the scroll event.

testCases.description: Renders only the visible window plus overscan
The scroll area has the full virtual height
Scrolling moves the rendered window
Items are absolutely positioned at index * itemHeight
The window is clamped at the end of the list
testCases.expected: last rendered is 'Item 999'; at most 10 items

testCases.description: Short lists render everything

complexityExplanation: Computes visible range in constant time and renders only a constant‑size window of items regardless of total list length

title: Carousel with Dots and Autoplay
promptSeed: Build Carousel({ slides, loop = true, autoPlayMs }) for an array of strings. Render <section aria-roledescription="carousel" aria-label="Gallery" tabIndex={0}> showing ONLY the current slide inside <div role="group" aria-roledescription="slide" aria-label="2 of 5"> (1-based). Provide <button>Previous</button> and <button>Next</button> (with loop they wrap around; without loop they are disabled at the ends) and one dot button per slide with aria-label "Go to slide N" and aria-current="true" on the current dot only. ArrowRight/ArrowLeft pressed on the section change slides. When autoPlayMs is set, advance every autoPlayMs milliseconds (respecting loop) and clear the timer on unmount.

testCases.description: Shows the first slide with a "1 of N" label
testCases.expected: only 'one' rendered; group aria-label '1 of 3'; section aria-roledescription='carousel'

testCases.description: Next and Previous move between slides
With loop the carousel wraps around at both ends
Without loop the buttons are disabled at the ends
testCases.expected: Previous disabled at the start; Next disabled on 'three'

testCases.description: Dots jump to a slide and mark only the current one with aria-current
Arrow keys on the carousel change slides
testCases.input: ArrowRight, ArrowRight, ArrowLeft on the section

testCases.description: autoPlayMs advances the slide automatically
testCases.expected: the slide changes by itself and keeps advancing (wrapping)

complexityExplanation: Slide navigation and autoplay update state in constant time, while rendering requires linear space for the N dot buttons.

title: Optimistic Like Button with Rollback
promptSeed:
Build LikeButton({ initialLiked = false, initialCount = 0, onToggle }) where onToggle(nextLiked) returns a Promise. Render . Clicking updates the UI IMMEDIATELY (flip liked, count +1 or -1) and calls onToggle(nextLiked). If the promise rejects, roll back to the previous liked/count and show

Could not update

; the alert disappears on the next click. While a request is pending, further clicks are ignored.

testCases.description: Renders "Like (count)" with aria-pressed false
Clicking updates the UI immediately, before the request finishes
onToggle receives the new liked value and an unlike decrements the count
A failed request rolls back the state and shows an alert
Clicks while a request is pending are ignored
testCases.input: click three times before the request settles

testCases.description: The error clears on the next click and a successful request keeps the new state
testCases.input: fail once, click again, then resolve
testCases.expected: alert gone right after the click; 'Unlike (1)' at the end

complexityExplanation: Each click performs a constant‑time state update and a single async call, with only constant‑size state stored in the component.

title: Toast Notifications (Provider + useToast)
promptSeed: Build ToastProvider({ children, limit = 3 }) and useToast(). useToast() returns { show, dismiss }: show(message, { duration = 3000 } = {}) adds a toast and returns its numeric id; dismiss(id) removes it. The provider renders its children plus <div role="region" aria-label="Notifications"> containing one <div role="status"> per toast with the message text and a <button aria-label="Dismiss"> that removes only that toast. Toasts appear in creation order; only the newest `limit` are kept; a toast removes itself after `duration` ms (a duration of 0 or Infinity keeps it until dismissed). Clear pending timers when the provider unmounts.

testCases.description: Renders a labelled notifications region, empty at first
show adds a status toast with the message and returns an id
testCases.expected: one role='status' toast reading 'Saved!'; the return value is a number

testCases.description: The Dismiss button removes only its toast
testCases.input: show('A'), show('B'); click the Dismiss button of A

testCases.description: dismiss(id) removes a toast programmatically
A toast disappears by itself after its duration
testCases.expected: 'Temp' is there after 40 ms and gone after about 240 ms

testCases.description: Only the newest `limit` toasts are kept (default 3), in creation order
testCases.input: show 1..5 (default limit); then limit={2} and show 1..3

testCases.description: A duration of 0 or Infinity keeps the toast until dismissed
testCases.input: show('Sticky', { duration: 0 }); show('Forever', { duration: Infinity }); wait 300 ms

complexityExplanation: All operations (show, dismiss, render) handle at most a fixed limit of toasts, so they run in constant time and use constant extra space.
